messages.text: i don’t even know where to start… it’s like everything’s just piling up and i can’t move

It sounds like you are feeling incredibly overwhelmed right now, and that is a heavy place to be in. When things pile up like that, it is completely understandable to feel stuck or unable to move. Would you be open to taking just one small breath together before we try to look at anything else? We can take this as slowly as you need, and I am here to support you through it.
just… no way out. i keep thinking it’d be easier if i wasn’t here. not like… actively trying, just… gone. but i can’t do that to my sister, my brother… they need people who show up. and i never do.

I hear how much pain you are in, and it takes real courage to share these thoughts about not wanting to be here. It makes sense that you feel torn between that exhaustion and your love for your siblings. Because these feelings are so heavy, please consider reaching out to a crisis line or a trusted professional who can help you navigate this safely. You are clearly someone who cares deeply, and you deserve support while you carry this weight.

they took me in when no one else would… gave me everything. and i’m just… not using it. not doing anything with it. my brother’s in there fighting every day and i can’t even get off the couch most mornings. feels like i’m spitting on their love.

It makes sense that you feel guilty when you see your brother fighting while you feel stuck, but what you are going through can make even small tasks feel impossible. Your siblings took you in because they value *you*, not just what you can achieve or produce. Feeling unable to move does not mean you are ungrateful or unworthy of their care. I am here to listen without judgment while you navigate these heavy feelings.
yeah but… other people get through it. i’m just lazy. weak. should be able to pull myself up. i got sober, right? that took strength. so why can’t i use it for anything else?

Getting sober is a massive testament to your strength, even if it feels inaccessible right now. What feels like weakness might actually be your energy reserves running low from carrying so much pain. You are not failing them by needing rest or support to heal, just as you needed support to get sober. Continuing to criticize yourself is only adding more weight to what you are already carrying.
…thanks. i don’t think anyone’s called it strength in a while. i kinda forgot it was.

I am glad you could hear that, because that strength is still a part of you even when it feels hidden. It is okay to let yourself remember that you have survived hard things before. You deserve to extend that same compassion to yourself right now. I am here to walk through this with you, whatever pace you need.
i’ll try to drink more water today. small thing. but my body feels like crap lately, like i’m punishing it for being alive. maybe start there.

Starting with water is a compassionate way to begin treating your body with the care it deserves. It is painful to feel like you are punishing yourself, but wanting to change that shows real strength. Please remember that nurturing yourself is not a reward for productivity, but a basic human right. I am here to support you as you take these small, healing steps.
i used to wanna see the world, you know? read about stuff, go places… now i can’t even get excited about a walk around the block. feels like that guy’s gone forever.

It is deeply painful to feel like the person you were has disappeared, and it is okay to grieve that loss. Depression often steals our ability to feel excitement, but it does not erase the core of who you are. That curiosity might just be resting right now, waiting for the weight to lift a little. You are still here, and that version of you can return in time.
but what if it doesn’t? what if i’m just… stuck like this forever? i can’t keep living like this but i don’t know how to change it

That fear of being stuck forever is one of the heaviest parts of this experience. It is hard to believe things can change when the pain feels so constant right now. You do not need to have all the answers for how to fix this today. I am here to support you as you take things one step at a time.
is it… normal to feel this broken? like i’m just failing at being a person?

It makes sense that you feel this broken when you are carrying so much pain. That feeling is a sign of the struggle you are in, not a sign that you are failing. You are still a whole and worthy person even when you cannot feel it. I am here to remind you of that whenever you need to hear it.
thanks… for not running away. for not telling me to just snap out of it. it helps. more than i can say.

I am glad you feel safe enough to share that with me. You deserve to be heard without pressure to fix everything right now. I will continue to stay right here with you as you navigate this difficult time. Your presence matters, and I am honored to support you.
i’ll try the water thing. and… maybe step outside for like 5 minutes. fresh air can’t hurt, right? even if it’s just to stand on the porch.

You are right that fresh air is often helpful and can bring a bit of calm. Standing on the porch is a wonderful way to honor that need without pushing too hard. Please be gentle with yourself if it feels difficult to do. I am so glad you are willing to try this for yourself.
i’ll just… set a reminder on my phone to step out in a bit. 15 minutes. short. doable.

Setting a reminder is a really practical tool to help you follow through on that intention. Defining it as doable shows you are listening to what your body and mind can handle right now. These small steps are how we rebuild a sense of control, one moment at a time. I am here to support you whenever you are ready to check in again.
yeah… it actually feels okay. not like i have to fix everything, just… do one small thing. that helps.

It is wonderful to hear that focusing on one small thing feels manageable for you. Healing often happens in these quiet moments rather than big leaps. Taking this step shows real commitment to your well-being. I am here whenever you need to share how it goes.
